questions.question: What does the passage compare the whole world to?
questions.answer: It compares the world to a well-run kingdom or city.

questions.question: How are things in the world shown in that picture of a kingdom?
questions.answer: They are shown as doing their jobs in an orderly way.

questions.question: What do the many groups in creation, from tiny things to stars, help show?
questions.answer: They help show Allah’s complete rule and power.

questions.question: Why does the passage say partners cannot share Allah’s rule?
questions.answer: Because one rule over all things cannot be shared without harm.

questions.question: What can happen when many hands try to do the same job?
questions.answer: Things get mixed up and confused.

questions.question: What example is given from human life to show that two rulers bring trouble?
questions.answer: Two kings in one land, or even two leaders in one area, bring disorder.

questions.question: What does the order in small and big things tell us?
questions.answer: It tells us that no partner is taking part in Allah’s work.

questions.question: Name one small thing and one big thing the passage uses to show order.
questions.answer: A fly’s wing and the lights in the sky.

questions.question: Why is sharing rule against the honor of sovereignty?
questions.answer: Because true kingship does not accept a rival.

questions.question: What does the passage say some people may do for a tiny bit of power?
questions.answer: They may hurt even close family for it.

questions.question: What does that human example help us understand about Allah’s rule?
questions.answer: If weak people guard small power so fiercely, Allah would never share His perfect rule.

questions.question: What is the main lesson of this whole passage?
questions.answer: Allah alone rules everything, and He has no partner.

questions.question: What title is given to this part of the passage?
questions.answer: It is about sovereignty.

questions.question: If someone studies the world carefully, what do they notice first?
questions.answer: They notice that it is organized and governed with wisdom.

questions.question: In the passage, what are creatures and parts of creation like?
questions.answer: They are like soldiers or groups in a great army.

questions.question: Which range of things is mentioned to show how wide Allah’s command is?
questions.answer: From tiny particles and plants and animals all the way to stars.

questions.question: What do these many ordered groups point to?
questions.answer: They point to one complete authority over all.

questions.question: Why would many gods make problems?
questions.answer: Because different rulers acting in the same place would ruin order.

questions.question: What word best fits a place with no order: peace, confusion, or kindness?
questions.answer: Confusion.

questions.question: What does the passage say we actually see in the world instead of confusion?
questions.answer: We see order everywhere.

questions.question: Where does the passage say this order can be seen?
questions.answer: In very tiny things and in huge things too.

questions.question: What does this order help us conclude about Allah’s actions?
questions.answer: No partner shares in them.

questions.question: Why does sovereignty refuse a rival, according to the passage?
questions.answer: Because rule has honor and dignity.

questions.question: How does the passage end its argument in a simple way?
questions.answer: Allah’s rule is absolute, so He does not share it with anyone.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the universe when looked at with care?
questions.answer: As active, successful, and wisely managed.

questions.question: What are all things described as doing?
questions.answer: They are obeying and carrying out their own tasks.

questions.question: Why does the passage mention armies?
questions.answer: To help us imagine the many parts of creation working under command.

questions.question: What kinds of things are included in these “armies”?
questions.answer: Very small things, plants, animals, and stars.

questions.question: What do these ordered “armies” show about Allah?
questions.answer: That His authority reaches everything.

questions.question: What is the result when many people try to control the same work?
questions.answer: The work becomes messy and mixed up.

questions.question: What happens in a place with two rulers, according to the passage?
questions.answer: Good order breaks down.

questions.question: What do we learn from the strong order in the world?
questions.answer: We learn that there is one ruler over it all.

questions.question: Why is the example of a fly and the sky important?
questions.answer: It shows that order is present in both tiny and huge parts of creation.

questions.question: What human weakness is mentioned in the passage?
questions.answer: People may fight cruelly for a small, temporary rule.

questions.question: What comparison is the passage making with that human weakness?
questions.answer: It shows that if weak humans cling to small rule, Allah would never share His perfect rule.

questions.question: What belief does this passage support for Muslims?
questions.answer: That Allah is One and has no partner.

questions.question: What big idea is taught in this passage?
questions.answer: Allah’s full kingship over everything.

questions.question: What picture is used to help explain this idea?
questions.answer: The picture of a kingdom or a city under strong rule.

questions.question: In that picture, how do created things act?
questions.answer: They act like obedient workers or soldiers.

questions.question: What does the passage say about commands in creation?
questions.answer: They reach all levels of creation.

questions.question: Does the passage describe the world as random or well ordered?
questions.answer: It describes it as well ordered.

questions.question: Why would more than one god not fit with that order?
questions.answer: Because shared control would bring disorder.

questions.question: What would happen to leadership if two leaders tried to run one place?
questions.answer: Leadership would turn into chaos.

questions.question: What proof from the world is given against that chaos?
questions.answer: The world shows neat order everywhere.

questions.question: How small and how large is this order?
questions.answer: It is in the tiniest parts and in the biggest heavenly bodies.

questions.question: Why is rivalry not accepted in sovereignty?
questions.answer: Because rulership has greatness and does not share its place.

questions.question: What does the passage say people may do for short-lived power?
questions.answer: They may act very cruelly.

questions.question: So what should we understand about Allah from all this?
questions.answer: Allah alone has the right and power to rule all things.

questions.question: When the passage talks about sovereignty, what does that mean here?
questions.answer: It means complete rule and authority.

questions.question: What does a careful person see in the universe?
questions.answer: A world run with wisdom and firmness.

questions.question: How are the parts of creation connected in the passage’s example?
questions.answer: They are connected like organized troops under command.

questions.question: What is one reason these examples are important?
questions.answer: They show that control over creation is united.

questions.question: What would many rulers over the same place cause?
questions.answer: They would cause disorder.

questions.question: What simple everyday idea is used to explain this?
questions.answer: One place cannot be run well by two top leaders.

questions.question: What do we really see in the universe instead?
questions.answer: We see harmony and order.

questions.question: What does harmony in both body cells and planets suggest?
questions.answer: One Lord is managing them all.

questions.question: According to the passage, can any partner step into Allah’s work?
questions.answer: No, there is no room for that.

questions.question: Why does the passage mention people wanting power?
questions.answer: To show that even weak humans do not like to share rule.

questions.question: What does that teach us about Allah’s sovereignty?
questions.answer: His sovereignty is far greater and never shared.

questions.question: What is the best short summary of the passage?
questions.answer: Order in all creation shows Allah rules alone.

questions.question: What does the passage say someone will see if they look at the cosmos very carefully?
questions.answer: They will see a world governed in a wise and busy way.

questions.question: What does every kind of thing in the world seem to be doing?
questions.answer: Each one is doing its own job.

questions.question: Why are atoms, plants, animals, and stars all mentioned together?
questions.answer: To show that Allah’s rule covers everything.

questions.question: What do these examples prove in the passage?
questions.answer: They prove one absolute sovereignty.

questions.question: What is the problem with many rulers in one task or one land?
questions.answer: It leads to confusion and loss of order.

questions.question: What does the passage say would happen if there were other gods besides Allah?
questions.answer: The heavens and the earth would be ruined.

questions.question: What do we see instead of ruin?
questions.answer: We see careful order everywhere.

questions.question: Give one example from the passage that shows tiny order.
questions.answer: The wing of a fly.

questions.question: Give one example from the passage that shows huge order.
questions.answer: The signs of the planets.

questions.question: What feeling about sovereignty is taught in the passage?
questions.answer: That it has dignity and does not accept an equal.

questions.question: How does the example of humans fighting for small power strengthen the message?
questions.answer: It makes it easier to understand that Allah’s perfect rule cannot be shared.

questions.question: What should a Muslim child learn from this passage about Allah?
questions.answer: Allah is the only true Ruler, and He has no partner.
